en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Nineteenth Chapter
Discussion on the Wholesome:
Is the element of nibbāna wholesome? Yes.
Is it with an object, and does it have turning toward it... pe ...and aspiration?
You should not say so...
pe ...Is it not rather without an object, and does it have no turning toward it... pe ...no aspiration?
“Yes.
“If it is without an object, then there is no turning toward it … nor aspiration for it. Therefore, indeed, you should not say:
‘The element of Nibbāna is wholesome.’”
Is non-greed wholesome, with an object, and does it have turning toward [it], ... [and so on] ...
aspiration? Yes.
Is the element of Nibbāna wholesome, with an object, and does it have turning toward it, ... [and so on] ... aspiration? [No.]
It should not be said thus … pe … non-hatred is wholesome … pe … non-delusion is wholesome … pe …
faith … energy … mindfulness …
“Is concentration … pe … wisdom wholesome and with an object? Is there, by means of that, turning toward … pe … aspiration?
“Yes.”
Is the element of Nibbāna wholesome and with an object, such that there is turning toward it … down to … aspiration?
One should not say so … [as before] … Is the element of Nibbāna wholesome and without an object, such that there is no turning toward it … down to … no aspiration?
“Yes,” you say.
“Is non-greed wholesome and without an object, and for it there is no turning toward [objects] …pe… nor aspiration?
You should not speak thus …pe…
Is the element of Nibbāna wholesome and without an object, and is there no turning toward it ... nor any aspiration for it?
Yes. Is non-hatred wholesome ... [and so on] ...? Yes.
Non-delusion is wholesome … [and so on] … faith … energy …
If mindfulness, concentration,
and so forth, up to wisdom, are wholesome and without an object, is there no turning toward [the object], and so forth, up to no aspiration through them?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Should it not be said that “the element of Nibbāna is wholesome”?
“Yes.
“Is it not the case that the element of Nibbāna is blameless?
“Yes.”
If the element of Nibbāna is blameless, then indeed it must be said:
“The element of Nibbāna is wholesome.
The Discussion on the Wholesome is finished.
